newsitem.title: JAPAN: Conoco consortium to drill test well off N.Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Conoco consortium to drill test well off N.Zealand.

text.p: A consortium of U.S., Japanese and New Zealand oil firms have decided to drill a test well in New Zealand's Offshore Northland Block having concluded seismic studies in the area, a partner in the project said on Monday.
Japan's Indonesia Petroleum Ltd (Inpex) said the consortium had notified the New Zealand government of its intention to drill a wildcat well in the Offshore Northland Block by August 1998.

Consortium members are Conoco Northland, a subsidiary of operator U.S. Conoco Inc, INPEX Northland Ltd, a subsidiary of Inpex, and New Zealand's Todd Petroleum Mining Co Ltd. The firms have a 56.67 percent, 33.33 percent and 10 percent stake respectively.
Conoco Inc is a unit of DuPont Co.
The Offshore Northland Block, which covers 113,898 square km and is up to 2,000 metres in depth, is off the northwest coast of New Zealand.
